{"sample_id": "blind-e9689eddc1c6479f9ed62c486194309c", "theorem": "Let $f$ be a continuous real function on a metric space $X$. Let $Z(f)$ (the zero set of $f$ ) be the set of all $p \in X$ at which $f(p)=0$. Prove that $Z(f)$ is closed.", "assumptions": [], "domain": "real_analysis", "explicit_subgoals": [], "candidate_text": "Since \(\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}\) is open, \(\{0\}\) is closed in \(\mathbb{R}\). Because \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous, the inverse image of every closed subset of \(\mathbb{R}\) is closed in \(X\). Therefore
\[
Z(f)=\{p\in X:f(p)=0\}=f^{-1}(\{0\})
\]
is closed in \(X\)."}
